did_you_know.text: The chapter opens with a direct request to the Lord: “Judge me.” The speaker asks the Lord to judge him, and alongside this request presents his integrity and his trust in the Lord.

Several verbs describing examination and refinement appear in this verse: “Test me,” “try me,” and “refine me.” In this way, the speaker asks the Lord to examine not only his actions but also his innermost being—“my kidneys and my heart.”
Mercy and truth are presented as the principles guiding the speaker’s life: “For your mercy is before my eyes; and I have walked in your truth.”

The speaker describes his separation from people characterized by falsehood, emptiness, or concealment: “men of falsehood” and “those who hide themselves.” In the next verse, he explicitly adds that he does not sit with evildoers or the wicked.
Washing the hands in innocence is mentioned alongside walking around the Lord’s altar. Together, these images connect personal purity with approaching the place where the Lord is worshiped.

The purpose of approaching the altar is described with three actions: proclaiming thanksgiving aloud and telling of all the Lord’s wonders. Thanksgiving includes both praise and testimony about the Lord’s deeds.

The speaker declares his love for “the dwelling place of your house” and “the place where your glory dwells.” This verse emphasizes his attachment to the holy place, not merely his desire to distance himself from wickedness.

The speaker asks not to be gathered together with sinners and men of bloodshed. This creates a clear contrast between his path, described as blameless and upright, and the ways of people characterized by deceit and bribery.

The chapter concludes with two images of stability and belonging: “My foot stands on level ground” and “In the assemblies I will bless the Lord.” The speaker asks to stand on an upright path and bless the Lord among the congregation.
